claims.explanation: Crizotinib selectively kills cells whose survival depends on the kinase activity of its targets ALK, MET, or ROS1, so sensitivity is best explained by genomic activation of these receptors (fusions, amplification, or activating mutation) rather than by any downstream mutation. The most-killed lines are enriched for MET mutation/amplification and for a transcriptional response resembling the ALK inhibitor NVP-TAE684, while the least-affected lines lack ALK/MET/ROS1 activation. Because the screen is a 5-day pooled viability assay, only lines with true oncogene addiction to ALK/MET/ROS1 show strong killing.

features.basis: ALK rearrangement/fusion is the validated crizotinib biomarker (PMID 20979469, 23724913, 25470694)
MET is a direct crizotinib target; MET-mutant/amplified lines (HGC27, HT115) are among the most killed
ROS1 rearrangement predicts crizotinib response (PMID 25264305, 22215748)
High MET expression/amplification increases dependence on MET signaling
High ALK expression/fusion transcript marks ALK-addicted tumors
ROS1 fusion-driven expression confers crizotinib sensitivity
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected (RKN, TCCPAN2, ASPC1) and lack ALK/MET/ROS1 addiction
BRAF-mutant lines (SNUC5, MFE319, G361) are among least affected, consistent with MAPK-driven, ALK-independent growth
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and may bypass receptor-tyrosine-kinase dependence
PIK3CA-mutant lines (MKN1, RT112, BT474) are among least affected, suggesting downstream PI3K activation bypasses ALK/MET blockade
NF1 loss causes RAS/MAPK activation and receptor-independent proliferation
CDKN2A loss is common in least-affected lines and may reflect general lack of ALK/MET/ROS1 addiction
